title: APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms
exclusions: Out of scope for non-APC chilled-water CRAC strings without traps or polls in the APC enterprise MIB tree, environments where SNMP from NMC to Splunk is disabled and no alternate poller exists, and pure predictive thermal analytics that do not ingest these SNMP feeds. Does not certify compliance with any specific regulation.
evidence: Scheduled saved search or alert "UC_15_1_31_APICoolingFault" against `index=power` with CSV export disabled but email/pdf digest to facilities; paired Dashboard Studio timeline and table panels filtered to `sourcetype=snmp:trap` or `snmp:apc:cooling`, retained per your internal evidence policy.

dataSources: `index=power` receives APC InRow and NetShelter airflow events as `sourcetype=snmp:trap` (enterprise `.1.3.6.1.4.1.318`) from Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) or as polled `sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling` metrics from the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537); key extracted fields include `trapoid`, `trap_name`, `eventName`, and cooling varbinds such as `coolingUnitState` when props are aligned to your MIB.
app: Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) trap receiver, SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537)

description: APC InRow and aisle containment products emit SNMP traps when compressors stall, fans fail, or airflow is inadequate. Landing those traps in Splunk gives the same early warning as UPS events for thermal runaway in edge and small data halls.
value: APC InRow and aisle containment products emit SNMP traps when compressors stall, fans fail, or airflow is i.... Timely UC-15.1.31 alerting on 'APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Stand up the trap path first: configure the Splunk Connect for SNMP (6266) receiver to accept UDP/162 from APC Network Management Card sources and confirm events write to `index=power` as `sourcetype=snmp:trap` with parsed `trapoid` and varbind alarm text into a consistent `alarm_text` or CIM-friendly field. For sites that poll instead of trap, define a modular input stanza in the SNMP Modular Input (1537) that walks the APC enterprise cooling OIDs and routes to `sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling`, extracting `coolingUnitState` and fan or compressor alarm OIDs documented in your MIB reference. Put a maintenance tag or host lookup in front of alerting so vendor-executed compressor tests during change windows do not page the default queue. Bind the alert action to the data-center facilities roster, attach the thermal escalation SOP, and keep a `-15m` dispatch window aligned to the cron schedule to match the SPL in this UC.
visualization: Dashboard Studio timeline of cooling trap volume on index=power by host; primary table sorted by _time with columns host, trapoid, trap_name, eventName, and parsed alarm_text; single-value KPI for distinct faulting InRow hosts in the last 15 minutes; markdown panel with NMC verification checklist for drilldown; optional Sankey or relationship visualization from trap host to row or aisle using an asset lookup.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `power`** — Planned work for 'APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-15.1.31. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `snmp:trap`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing configured threshold. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `power` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `snmp:trap`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise 9.2+ or Splunk Cloud search tier with a Heavy Forwarder or dedicated data-collection node hosting either Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) or the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537).
• RBAC: use a `splunk_admin` (or deployment-manager equivalent) principal to install apps and open `inputs.conf`; grant the operations team a custom role with read access to `index=power` and `edit_monitor` disabled in production.
• Network/firewall: allow SNMP traps (UDP/162) from APC InRow/NMC subnets to the collector; for polling, allow SNMP GET/GET-NEXT (UDP/161) outbound from Splunk to each NMC.

Configure data collection
• Trap path: bind the SC4SNMP listener to the correct interface, register each APC device IP, and verify the first replayed trap shows `sourcetype=snmp:trap` on `index=power` with `trapoid` containing `.1.3.6.1.4.1.318`.
• Enable rich parsing (`full_json`, `VARBINDS`, or equivalent) so `trap_name`, `eventName`, and raw varbind strings are searchable for keywords like compressor, fan, airflow, or InRow.
• Polling path: create an SNMP Modular Input profile with a 60–120s interval, normalize output to `sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling`, and confirm `coolingUnitState` plus fault OIDs populate after a walk of the APC enterprise branch.

Create and tune the correlation
• Start from the packaged SPL baseline: constrain to `host=*`, `trapoid="*318*"`, and (for dual path) `(sourcetype=snmp:trap OR sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling)`.
• Add `streamstats` or `transaction` keyed by host and trap signature inside a `-15m` window to collapse flap duplicates before alerting.
• Optional: `lookup` enrich host -> row ID so dashboards separate aisle containment zones.

Validate
• Replay a sanitized trap `_raw` sample in search using `index=power sourcetype=snmp:trap` over `-24h@h` and compare timestamps with the APC web UI alarm history on the same NMC.
• For polled feeds, chart `_time` vs `coolingUnitState` and confirm gaps align with SNMP timeouts rather than silent drops.

Operationalize and troubleshoot
• Route alerts to facilities on-call with throttle keyed on host + trap signature; attach links to rack inlet temperature dashboards.
• If dual-published to a BMS, document precedence (Splunk vs BMS source of truth) to avoid duplicate tickets.
• Common failures: SNMP ACL changes on NMC (symptom: sudden zero events), clock skew (symptom: traps appear outside drill windows), SC4SNMP restart clearing dedup state (symptom: alert storm) — capture in the runbook with restart and ACL checks.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the physical data center for power, cooling, environment, and physical access.
